nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱذْكُرْ فِي ٱلْكِتَابِ مُوسَىٰ إِنَّهُ كَانَ مُخْلِصاًً﴾.
That is: We purified him (akhlaṣnāhu) and made him chosen, pure of defilement.
And the meaning of "مُخْلِصاً" with a kasra on the lām is: he affirmed the oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, by obeying Him, and purified himself of defilement.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَرَّبْنَاهُ نَجِيّاً﴾.
Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUmar al-Kūfī narrated to us: Hannād narrated to us: Wakīʿ and Qabīṣa narrated to us from Sufyān, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning the saying of Allah ﴿وَقَرَّبْنَاهُ نَجِيّاً﴾; he said: He was brought near until he heard the scratching of the Pen.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱذْكُرْ فِي ٱلْكِتَابِ إِدْرِيسَ إِنَّهُ كَانَ صِدِّيقاً نَّبِيَّاً. وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَاناً عَلِيّاً﴾ [verses 56 and 57].
It is said: He asked the Angel of Death to show him the Fire, so he showed it to him; then he asked him to admit him into Paradise, so he admitted him into it; then he said to him: Come out. He said: How shall I come out, when Allah has said ﴿وما هم منها بمخرجين﴾ ("nor will they be removed from it")?!
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is possible that Allah informed Idrīs of this, and then the Qurʾān was revealed with it.
And it is said that its meaning is: in standing and rank.
More sound than these two views, because of the high quality of its chain of transmission (isnād) and its soundness, is what Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: Anas ibn Mālik [narrated] from Mālik ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿa that the Prophet ﷺ, when he was taken on the Night Journey, said: "I saw Idrīs in the fourth heaven." «[Translator's note: the Arabic as printed reads «أنس بن مالك بن صعصعة», but the well-known chain is Anas ibn Mālik from Mālik ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿa; the source text is as given.]»
And Sufyān narrated from Hārūn, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī: ﴿وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَاناً عَلِيّاً﴾ — he said: The fourth heaven.
And al-Aʿmash narrated from Shimr ibn ʿAṭiyya, from Hilāl ibn Isāf, who said: We were with Kaʿb al-Aḥbār when ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās came forward. He said: This is the cousin of your Prophet. So we made room for him, and he said: O Kaʿb, what is the meaning of ﴿وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَاناً عَلِيّاً﴾? Kaʿb said: Idrīs ﷺ had a friend among the angels, and Allah revealed to him: I raise up for you every day the like of the deeds of the people of the earth. So Idrīs said to the angel: Speak for me to the Angel of Death, so that he may delay taking my soul. So the angel carried him under the edge of his wing, and when he reached the fourth heaven he met the Angel of Death and spoke to him. He said: Where is he? He said: Here he is. He said: How strange! I was commanded to take his soul in the fourth heaven. So he took it there.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَخَلَفَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌٌ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayd said: Ḥajjāj narrated to us from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, who said: That is at the coming of the Hour, when the righteous of this community — the community of Muḥammad — have gone; they will leap upon one another in the alleyways in fornication.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-khalf with a sukūn on the lām is used only for what is bad, as Labīd said:
ذَهَبَ الَّذِينَ يُعَاشُ في أكْنَافِهِمْ * وبَقَيِتُ في خَلْفٍ كجِلْدِ الأَجْرَبِ
(Gone are those in whose shelter one could live, and I remain among a worthless remnant (khalf) like the hide of a mangy camel.)
But if you say khalaf with a vowel on the lām, it is for what is good, as it is said: "May Allah make in you a worthy successor (khalaf) to your father."
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَضَاعُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ ٱلشَّهَوَاتِ﴾.
Al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymira said: "They neglected it" means: they delayed it beyond its time; had they abandoned it, they would have disbelieved.
And it is said: They neglected it means they abandoned it altogether.
And this is more likely, because of His saying afterwards ﴿إلاَّ مَنْ تَابَ وَآمَنَ﴾, and this indicates that they had disbelieved.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَلْقُونَ غَيّاً﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿUbayda, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: It is a valley in Hell.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied sense (taqdīr) according to the people of the language is: they will meet the recompense of error (ghayy), just as He, exalted be His mention, said ﴿وَمَنْ يَفْعَل ذَلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثَامَاً﴾.
And it is possible that the valley is called ghayy because those who go astray (al-ghāwūn) end up in it.

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ ٱلَّتِي وَعَدَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ عِبَادَهُ بِٱلْغَيْبِِ﴾.
Gardens of abiding. It is said: ʿadana bi-l-makān, when one stays in a place; and from it the word "maʿdin" (a mine) was used, because its people stay at it winter and summer and do not move away from it in search of pasture.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ وَعْدُهُ مَأْتِيّاً﴾.
"Maʾtiyy" is the passive participle (mafʿūl) from ityān (coming); and everything that reaches you, you have also reached it, as you say: Good reached me from so-and-so, and I reached good from him.
So one who is weak in Arabic says: "mafʿūl" here is in the sense of "fāʿil".

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَّ يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْواً إِلاَّ سَلاَماً﴾.
Al-laghw: falsehood, that in which there is sin, and that which has no meaning.
And al-salām: everything that is safe from that; it is a noun comprising all good, i.e. they hear nothing but everything they love.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَهُمْ رِزْقُهُمْ فِيهَا بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيّاً﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: In the measures of night and day.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of this is that in Paradise there is no morning and no evening, but the meaning is: in the measures of these times.
And Qatāda said: Among the Arabs, when a man found something to eat in the morning and the evening, he was delighted with it; so Allah informed them that this would be in Paradise.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا نَتَنَزَّلُ إِلاَّ بِأَمْرِ رَبِّكَ لَهُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِينَا وَمَا خَلْفَنَا وَمَا بَيْنَ ذٰلِكََ﴾.
ʿAmr ibn Dharr narrated from his father, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said to Gabriel, peace be upon him: "Why do you not visit us more than you visit us?" So Allah revealed: ﴿وَمَا نَتَنَزَّلُ إِلاَّ بِأَمْرِ رَبِّكَ﴾ to the end of the verse, and this was the answer to him.
And Abū Ḥaṣīn narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning His saying, exalted is He, ﴿مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِينَا﴾: he said: of the affair of the Hereafter; ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَنَا﴾: of the affair of this world; ﴿وَمَا بَيْنَ ذٰلِكَ﴾: what is between this world and the Hereafter, i.e. the barzakh (the intermediate realm).
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ نَسِيّاً﴾.
It is said its meaning is: He has not forgotten you, even if the revelation was delayed for you.
And it is said: He knows what has been, and what will be — and has not yet occurred — and what is coming to be; [His knowledge] is not cut off; He preserves it and has forgotten nothing of it.

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُ سَمِيّاً﴾.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Do you know anyone besides Him who is named al-Raḥmān?
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the most eminent chain of transmission I know to have been narrated about this word, and it is a sound view: "al-Raḥmān" is said only of Allah, while "raḥīm" may be said of other than Allah.
We have already explained why "al-Raḥmān" is said only of Allah, in Sūrat al-Ḥamd.
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُ سَمِيّاً﴾? He said: a like.
And Ḥajjāj narrated from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُ سَمِيّاً﴾ — he said: He has no partner, no like.
And it is said: Do you know anyone to whom you say "Allah" other than Him?
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close to one another.
Rather, the meaning is: Do you know anyone to whom this is said by right, other than Allah? For He is the One whose mercy encompasses everything, and He is the All-Powerful, the Provider.
And it is said the meaning is: His name mentioned in this verse is not given to anyone else, and it is ﴿رَبُّ السَّموات والأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُما﴾.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَقُولُ ٱلإِنْسَانُ أَإِذَا مَا مِتُّ لَسَوْفَ أُخْرَجُ حَيّاً. أَوَلاَ يَذْكُرُ ٱلإِنْسَٰنُ﴾.
That is: Does he not reflect and consider, and recall it with knowledge, and make it clear to himself?

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَوَرَبِّكَ لَنَحْشُرَنَّهُمْ وَٱلشَّيَاطِينَ ثُمَّ لَنُحْضِرَنَّهُمْ حَوْلَ جَهَنَّمَ جِثِيّاًً﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: That is, on their knees.
And the meaning is: because of the severity of what they are in, they are unable to stand.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ لَنَنزِعَنَّ مِن كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ عَلَى ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ عِتِيّاً﴾.
Sufyān narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, who said: Those greatest in crime will be begun with.
And the meaning of this view is: We begin by punishing the greatest of them in crime, then the one who comes next, then the one who comes next.
Mujāhid said: ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ﴾: [from every community; ﴿عِتِيَّاً﴾] i.e. in disbelief.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِن مِّنكُمْ إِلاَّ وَارِدُهَا كَانَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ حَتْماً مَّقْضِيّاً﴾.
There are five views on this verse:
a- It is said that coming to it (wurūd) means entering it, because after it comes ﴿وَنَذَرُ الظَّالِمينَ فِيهَا﴾.
And ﴿نَذَرُ﴾ ("We leave") is said only of what has taken place; so Allah saves those who were God-fearing, and they go on to His mercy, and they know the measure of what they were delivered from, because they had entered the Fire and been delivered from it. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, and its chain of transmission is good.
Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās and Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq disputed. Nāfiʿ said: Coming to it is not entering. Ibn ʿAbbās said: It is entering. Have you considered the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿إنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ أَنْتُمْ لَهَا وَارِدُونَ﴾?
Did they come to it [i.e. enter it] or not? And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿وَبِئْسَ الوِرْدُ المَوْرُودُ﴾. As for me and you, we shall come to it, and I hope that Allah will bring me out of it, and that He will not bring you out of it because of your denial. «[Translator's note: the Arabic as printed reads «فقال لنافع: ليس الورود الدخول», literally "he said to Nāfiʿ"; the context shows that it is Nāfiʿ who denies that wurūd means entering.]» Then Nāfiʿ said to him: ﴿رَبَّنَا إنَّكَ مَنْ تُدْخِلِ النَّارَ فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَه﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Whoever has three [children] die who had not reached the age of responsibility, the Fire will not touch him except for the fulfilment of the oath."
Meaning: the coming to it (wurūd).
b- And it is said: The believers come to it while it is frozen still.
Sufyān narrated from Thawr ibn Yazīd, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, who said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, they will say: O Lord, did You not promise us that we would come to the Fire? He will say: You did come to it, while it was frozen still."
c- And it is said: It means the Resurrection.
d- And it is said: ﴿وَإِن مِّنكُمْ إِلاَّ وَارِدُهَا﴾ is meant of the polytheists; the holder of this view adduced as evidence that ʿUmar ibn al-Walīd narrated from ʿIkrima that he read ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْهُم إِلاَّ وَارِدُهَا﴾ ("there is none of them but will come to it").
e- And the fifth view: that coming to it means reaching it and passing by it.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إلاَّ وارِدُهَا﴾ — he said: passing by it.
And al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim narrated from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmayr: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إلاَّ وَارِدُهَا﴾.
He said: being present at it.
These, then, are five views, and Allah knows best what He intended; except that it is well known in the speech of the Arabs to say: waradtu such-and-such, meaning I reached it without entering it. Zuhayr said:
فَلَمَّا وَرَدْنَ المَاءَ زُرْقَاً جِمَامُهُ * وَضَعْنَ عِصِيَّ الحَاضِرِ المُتَخَيِّمِ
(When they came to (waradna) the water, its pools blue and clear, they set down the staves of one who settles and pitches his tent.)
And Ubayy ibn Kaʿb read ﴿ثُمَّ نُنَحِّي الِّذِينَ اتقوْا﴾ ("then We shall remove those who were God-fearing"), i.e. in that place.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The clearest of these views is the view of the one who said that ﴿وَإنْ مِنْكُمْ إلاَّ وارِدُهَا﴾ refers to the Resurrection; His saying ﴿فَوَرَبِّكَ لَنَحْشُرَنَّهُمْ﴾ indicates the mention of the Resurrection, so He alluded to it thus.
Likewise the mention of Hell indicates the Resurrection, because it is in it; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says: ﴿لاَ خَوفٌ عَلَيهمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يَحْزَنُون﴾, so it is unlikely that entering the Fire could go together with this.
And Ibn ʿAbbās read: ﴿ثُمَّ نُنْجِي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا، ونَذَرُ الظَّالِمِينَ فِيهَا جِثِيَّاً﴾.

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُنَا بَيِّنَٰتٍ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَيُّ ٱلْفَرِيقَيْنِ خَيْرٌ مَّقَاماً وَأَحْسَنُ نَدِيّاًً﴾.
Abū Ẓibyān narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying ﴿أَيُّ ٱلْفَرِيقَيْنِ خَيْرٌ مَّقَاماً﴾: he said: in dwelling; ﴿وَأَحْسَنُ نَدِيّاً﴾: he said: in assembly.
Al-Kisāʾī said: al-nadiyy and al-nādī mean the assembly.
Abū Jaʿfar said: That is well known in the language; it is said: nadawtu al-qawma andūhum, i.e. I gathered them; and from it "Dār al-Nadwa" (the House of Assembly) was so called, because they used to gather in it when a matter troubled them; and from it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿وَتَأْتُونَ فِي نَادِيكُمُ المُنْكَرَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:74-74.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِّن قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَحْسَنُ أَثَاثاً وَرِءْياًً﴾.
Al-Aʿmash narrated from Abū Ẓibyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-athāth is household goods, and al-riʾy is outward appearance.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-athāth in the language is household goods. Al-Aḥmar said: its singular is athātha.
And al-Farrāʾ said: It has no singular.
Likewise al-riʾy is outward appearance, from raʾaytu (I saw), i.e. what you see of a person's form and clothing. It is also read ﴿ورِيَّاً﴾ without a hamza, and that is good, by lightening the hamza.
And it is good here so that the verse endings match.
And it is possible that it is from al-riyy (being well watered) and comfort.
And al-Akhfash said: It is possible that it is from the watering (riyy) of rain. And al-ziyy with zāy means appearance and beauty; it is said: zayyatu al-marʾa, i.e. I adorned her and made her ready.

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ مَن كَانَ فِي ٱلضَّلاَلَةِ فَلْيَمْدُدْ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ مَدّاً﴾.
It may be asked: What is the meaning of the imperative here?
Abū Jaʿfar said: The answer is that this is more emphatic. If you said: "If you come to me, then let me honour you (fa-l-ukrimka)", it would be more emphatic than your saying: "If you come to me, I will honour you (fa-ukrimuka)"; and it became more emphatic only because it contains the sense of binding obligation.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا رَأَوْاْ مَا يُوعَدُونَ إِمَّا ٱلعَذَابَ وَإِمَّا ٱلسَّاعَةَ﴾.
The punishment here is that Allah gives the Muslims victory over them, so that they punish them with killing and captivity.
And the Hour is the Resurrection, i.e.: or the Resurrection takes place and they go to the Fire. ﴿فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ هُوَ شَرٌّ مَّكَاناً﴾ — when they go to the Fire; ﴿وَأَضْعَفُ جُنداً﴾ — when Allah gives the Muslims victory over them.

nahhas-meani:76-76.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَزِيدُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱهْتَدَواْ هُدًى﴾.
It is said: We increase them in guidance through the abrogating and the abrogated.
And it is said: We increase them in guidance as a recompense.
We have already mentioned the meaning of ﴿وَٱلْبَاقِيَاتُ ٱلصَّالِحَاتُ﴾ in Sūrat al-Kahf.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي كَفَرَ بِآيَاتِنَا وَقَالَ لأُوتَيَنَّ مَالاً وَوَلَداً﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Salām narrated to us: Abū al-Azhar narrated to us: Rawḥ ibn ʿUbāda narrated to us: Shuʿba narrated to us from Sulaymān, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, from Khabbāb, who said: "I was a blacksmith in the Jāhiliyya, and I did work for al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil until some dirhams owed to me by him had accumulated. So I came to claim them from him, and he said: I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muḥammad ﷺ. I said: I will not disbelieve in Muḥammad until you die and are resurrected. He said: And will I be resurrected? I said: Yes. He said: Then I shall have wealth and children there, and I will pay you." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي كَفَرَ بِآيَاتِنَا وَقَالَ لأُوتَيَنَّ مَالاً وَوَلَداً﴾?! to the end of the story.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the sense of the ḥadīth.

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
On His saying, exalted is He: ﴿أَمِ ٱتَّخَذَ عِندَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ عَهْداًً﴾.
There are several views:
Sufyān said: a righteous deed.
And it is said: the covenant (ʿahd) here is affirming the oneness of Allah and believing in Him.
And it is said: the covenant here is the promise of what he said.
And al-Aswad ibn Yazīd said: ʿAbd Allāh said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, will say on the Day of Resurrection: "Whoever has a covenant with Me, let him stand." They said: O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, then teach us. He said: Say: "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, I make a covenant with You in this worldly life: if You entrust me to my own deeds, You bring me near to evil and keep me far from good; and I trust in nothing but Your mercy. So make it a covenant for me with You which You will fulfil for me on the Day of Resurrection; indeed You do not break the promise."
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close to one another. And ʿahd in the language may mean safe-conduct; from it come "the people of the covenant" (ahl al-ʿahd), and from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿قَالَ لاَ يَنَالُ عَهْدِي الظَّالِمينَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayd said: It is as though He said: I will not give them safety from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.
Likewise is the view of Qatāda; he said: in the Hereafter; as for this world, they have eaten and drunk, lived and seen.
So if affirming the oneness [of Allah] is called a covenant, it is because one is made safe by it; and likewise the promise.

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَرِثُهُ مَا يَقُولُ وَيَأْتِينَا فَرْداًً﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, We shall inherit from him what he has, i.e. his saying ﴿لأُوتَيَنَّ مَالاً وَوَلَداً﴾.
He said: And in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: ﴿وَنرِثُهُ مَا عندهَ﴾ ("and We shall inherit from him what he has").
And it is said: We shall keep the sin upon him, so it is as though it were inherited.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is said that this is explained in the ḥadīth of Khabbāb; and it is said: the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: We shall strip him of his wealth and children on the Day of Resurrection; do you not see that after it comes ﴿وَيَأْتِينَا فَرْداً﴾?!
Abū Jaʿfar said: The soundest of what has been said about this is that the meaning of ﴿وَنَرِثُهُ مَا يَقُولُ﴾ is: We preserve against him what he says, until We pay him in full his punishment for it.
And of this kind is the ḥadīth of Abū al-Dardāʾ from the Prophet ﷺ: "The scholars are the heirs of the prophets."
And of it is: ﴿وَأَورثكم أَرْضَهُمْ وَدِيَارهُمْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ آلِهَةً لِّيَكُونُواْ لَهُمْ عِزّاً﴾.
That is, helpers.

nahhas-meani:82-82.t:
Then He said, glory be to Him: ﴿كَلاَّ سَيَكْفُرُونَ بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ﴾.
"Kallā", according to the people of Arabic, is divided into two kinds:
One of them: that it is a deterrent and a call to attention, and a rejection of a statement; and so it is here, i.e. desist from this, and take notice of the error in it.
When it is like this, the pause on it is a complete pause (al-tamām).
And it may be a deterrent and a call to attention without being a rejection of a statement, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿كَلاَّ إِنَّ الإِنْسَانَ لَيَطْغَى﴾.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدّاً﴾.
That is, helpers [against them].
Mujāhid said: That is, their idols will be against them in the Fire, disputing with them and calling them liars.

nahhas-meani:83-83.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا ٱلشَّيَاطِينَ عَلَى ٱلْكَافِرِينَ تَؤُزُّهُمْ أَزّاًً﴾.
There are two views on its meaning:
One of them: You did not protect them from the devils.
And the other view: We assigned the devils to them, as a recompense for their disbelief. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ومَنْ يَعْشُ عَنْ ذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَنِ نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطَاناً﴾.
And the meaning of ﴿أَرْسَلْنُّا﴾ in the language here is: We gave [them] power over. «[Translator's note: the source prints the word as «أَرْسَلْنُّا»; the Qurʾānic text reads «أَرْسَلْنَا».]»
Then He said, glory be to Him: ﴿تَؤُزُّهُمْ أَزّاً﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: They incite them vigorously.
Ibn Jurayj said: The devils drive the disbelievers on to evil: Go on, go on! — until they cast them into the Fire.
Qatāda said: ﴿تَؤُزُّهُمْ﴾, i.e. they agitate them toward acts of disobedience.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close in meaning. Its origin is from azaztu al-shayʾa aʾuzzuhu azzan wa-azīzan, i.e. I moved it; and from it is the ḥadīth: "The Prophet ﷺ used to pray, and there was a seething (azīz) in his chest like the seething of a boiling pot" — i.e. from weeping.

nahhas-meani:84-84.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلاَ تَعْجَلْ عَلَيْهِمْ إِنَّمَا نَعُدُّ لَهُمْ عَدّاً﴾.
Hushaym narrated from Abū Yazīd, from Abū Jaʿfar "Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī", concerning His saying, exalted is He, ﴿إِنَّمَا نَعُدُّ لَهُمْ عَدّاً﴾: he said: everything, even the breaths.

nahhas-meani:85-85.t:
His saying, majestic is His name: ﴿يَوْمَ نَحْشُرُ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ إِلَى ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ وَفْداًً﴾.
The people of exegesis said: That is, riding.
Al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah's good pleasure be upon him, recited ﴿يَوْمَ نَحْشُرُ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ إِلَى ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ وَفْداً﴾ and said: "By Allah, they will not be gathered on their feet; rather they will be brought she-camels the like of which creation has never seen, with saddles of gold upon them and reins of chrysolite; then they will set off with them to Paradise, until they knock at its gate."

nahhas-meani:86-86.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَسُوقُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ وِرْداً﴾.
The people of exegesis said: That is, thirsty.
The people of the language said: It is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of waradtu (I came to water), so the implied form (taqdīr) according to them is: "possessors of a coming to water (dhawī wird)".
And they have reported that those who come to water are called "wird"; so since they come to the Fire as the thirsty come to water, they were called "wird". On this basis it agrees with the language.

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَّ يَمْلِكُونَ ٱلشَّفَاعَةَ إِلاَّ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ عِندَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ عَهْداً﴾.
If you make "man" a badal (substitute) for the wāw [of the plural], the meaning is:
None possesses intercession except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, for he will intercede.
And if you make it an exception not from the first [kind] (i.e. a disjoined exception), the meaning is:
But whoever has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful — intercession will be made on his behalf.

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالُواْ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ وَلَداً. لَّقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئاً إِدّاً﴾ [verses 88 and 89].
Mujāhid said: That is, something enormous.
And that is well known in the language; it is said: jāʾa shayʾan iddan, and jāʾa bi-shayʾin iddin (he came with a monstrous thing).
And Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read ﴿أَدَّاً﴾ with a fatḥa on the hamza.
The kasra is better known.
Abū ʿUbayd said: And from it is the report that when ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muljam — may Allah curse him — resolved to kill ʿAlī, may Allah's good pleasure be upon him, he discussed it with so-and-so — Abū ʿUbayd said: and he named him — who said: May your mother be bereft of you! You have come with a monstrous thing (iddan). Would you kill ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib?

nahhas-meani:90-90.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَكَادُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: al-infiṭār is splitting.
Abū Jaʿfar said: That is well known in the language; it is said: faṭara nābu al-baʿīr (the camel's tooth broke through), when the flesh splits and it comes out.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَخِرُّ ٱلْجِبَالُ هَدّاً﴾.
That is, in collapse.

nahhas-meani:91-91.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَن دَعَوْا لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ وَلَداًً﴾.
That is: because they ascribed a son to the Most Merciful, and: from their ascribing [a son].

nahhas-meani:96-96.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ سَيَجْعَلُ لَهُمُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ وُدّاً﴾.
Mujāhid narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: love.
Mujāhid said: Allah loves them and makes them beloved to His creation.

nahhas-meani:97-97.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَاهُ بِلِسَانِكََ﴾.
That is: We have made it easy, and sent it down in your language.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتُنْذِرَ بِهِ قَوْماً لُّدّاً﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Ismāʿīl, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: crooked away from the truth.
And Mujāhid said: al-aladd is the wrongdoer who does not go straight.
And al-Ḥasan said: al-ludd are the deaf.
And Abū ʿUbayda said: He is the one who does not accept the truth and claims falsehood; and he recited:
إِنَّ تَحْتَ الأحْجَارِ حَدّاً وَلِينَاً * وخَصِيِمَاً أَلَدَّ ذَا مِغْلاَقِ
(Beneath the stones lie sharpness and gentleness, and a fiercely contentious (aladd) disputant who could shut [every argument].)
And it is also narrated as "miʿlāq" with ʿayn.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The best of these views is the first. And al-ladīdān are the two sides of the neck, so it is as though it were a figurative image.

nahhas-meani:98-98.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِّن قَرْنٍ هَلْ تُحِسُّ مِنْهُمْ مِّنْ أَحَدٍ﴾.
It is said: hal aḥsasta ṣāḥibaka? i.e. did you see your companion?
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوْ تَسْمَعُ لَهُمْ رِكْزاً﴾.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: a sound.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-rikz in the language is the faint sound that can hardly be made out.
And may Allah bless the best of His creation, Muḥammad His Prophet, and his family, and grant them peace.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Exalted be His name: ﴿كۤهيعۤصۤ﴾.
Abū Bakr ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us; he said: Salama ibn Shabīb narrated to us; he said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us; he said: Ibn ʿUyayna informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning the saying of the Exalted ﴿كۤهيعۤصۤ﴾, that he said: Kāf is from «كافٍ» (Sufficient), Hāʾ from «هادٍ» (Guide), Yāʾ from «حكيم» (Wise), ʿAyn from «عليم» (All-Knowing), and Ṣād from «صادق» (Truthful).
ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: And Maʿmar informed us from Qatāda concerning His saying ﴿كۤهيعۤصۤ﴾ that he said: It is one of the names of the Qurʾān.
Abū Jaʿfar said: We have dealt exhaustively with this matter in Sūrat al-Baqara.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُ نِدَآءً خَفِيّاًً﴾.
Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd said: Al-Ḥasan held that the imam should supplicate in the qunūt and those behind him should say "Āmīn", without raising the voice; and Yūnus recited ﴿إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُ نِدَآءً خَفِيّاً﴾.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّي وَهَنَ ٱلْعَظْمُ مِنِّي﴾.
Abū Zayd said: One says «وَهَنَ، يَهِنُ» and «وَهِنَ يَوْهَنُ».
Someone else said: That is, it became weak.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱشْتَعَلَ ٱلرَّأْسُ شَيْباً﴾.
Of one in whose head grey hair has become abundant, it is said: «اشتعلَ رأسهُ شيباً» ("his head has blazed with grey hair").
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَمْ أَكُنْ بِدُعَآئِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيّاً﴾.
That is, I have never been disappointed when I called upon You.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإِنِّي خِفْتُ ٱلْمَوَالِيَ مِن وَرَآئِي﴾.
Hishām related from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: [المَوالي are] the kalāla (collateral heirs).
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: the ʿaṣaba (agnatic heirs).
Abū ʿUbayda said: He means the paternal cousins; and he said: ﴿مِنْ وَرَائي﴾ means "in front of me".
Mujāhid's view is preferable: the ʿaṣaba are called «موالٍ», i.e. those who are next to him in lineage, just as the relatives (الأقرباء) are those who are near to him in lineage.
The paternal cousins are included in this, as the poet said:
* "مَهْلاً بَني عَمِّنَا مَهْلاً مَوَالِينَا" *
("Gently, O sons of our paternal uncle; gently, O our kinsmen!")
And his saying also that ﴿مِنْ وَرَائي﴾ means "in front of me" contradicts the view of the exegetes, because for them the meaning is: after my death.
Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān — Allah's mercy be upon him — dictated to me ﴿وَإِنِّي خَفَّتِ المَوَالي مِنْ وَرَائِي﴾, meaning with a doubled fāʾ, a kasra on the tāʾ and a sukūn on the yāʾ; and he said: its meaning is "have become few".
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَكَانَتِ ٱمْرَأَتِي عَاقِراً﴾.
That is, she does not give birth, as though she had a wound (عَقْر) preventing her from childbearing.
And it is related that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read ﴿عُسِيّاً﴾.
One says «عتا يعتو» and «عَسَى يَعْسُو» when someone reaches the extreme in hardness and old age.
Qatāda said: He was some seventy-odd years old.
[Translator's note: the remark on ﴿عُسِيّاً﴾ concerns «عِتِيّاً» in verse 8, but it stands here in the source.]

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَرِثُنِي وَيَرِثُ مِنْ آلِ يَعْقُوبََ﴾.
Hushaym related from Ismāʿīl, from Abū Khālid, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: He would be a prophet, as they were prophets.
[Translator's note: the chain reads «عن إسماعيل، عن أبي خالد» in the source; in the previous entry the same transmitter is Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid. Translated as written.]
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: His inheritance was knowledge, and Zakariyyā was of the family of Jacob.
And it is related from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind from al-Ḥasan: ﴿يرثني﴾, i.e. he inherits my wealth, ﴿وَيَرِثُ مِنْ آلِ يَعْقُوبَ﴾: the prophethood.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] holds the first view: it is unlikely that a prophet would be anxious about his wealth being inherited, because of the transmitted ḥadīth.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰزَكَرِيَّآ إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلاَمٍ ٱسْمُهُ يَحْيَىٰ﴾.
That is, We said: O Zakariyyā.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيّاً﴾.
Isrāʾīl related from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: No one before Yaḥyā was named Yaḥyā besides him.
Sufyān related from his father, from Ḥassān ibn Abī al-Ashras: ﴿لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيّاً﴾ — he said: an equal.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: a like.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What strengthens this is that the exegetes, among them Ibn Jurayj, said concerning the saying of Allah ﴿هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُ سَمِيّاً﴾: i.e. a like, i.e. a partner.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ ٱلْكِبَرِ عِتِيّاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, thinness (wasting) of the bones.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِي غُلاَمٌٌ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: He wanted to know in what way a child would be born to him, when his wife was barren and he had grown old.
Abū Jaʿfar said: We have already mentioned «العاقر» and «العِتِيّ» before this.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قَالَ كَذٰلِكَ قَالَ رَبُّكَ هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ﴾.
That is, the matter is as you have been told.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِن قَبْلُ وَلَمْ تَكُ شَيْئاً﴾.
That is, an existing thing.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ ٱجْعَل لِيۤ آيَةً﴾.
That is, a sign indicating the occurrence of what I have been given glad tidings of.
﴿قَالَ آيَتُكَ أَلاَّ تُكَلِّمَ ٱلنَّاسَ ثَلاَثَ لَيَالٍ سَوِيّاً﴾.
ʿIkrima, Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, without being mute.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ مِنَ ٱلْمِحْرَابِِ﴾.
The exegetes said: It was an elevated place.
And so it is according to the lexicographers: it is as though it were on a «حَرْبة» (spear-point) because of its height; and from this the place in which one prays is called «محراب», as though it were the highest part of the assembly.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَأَوْحَىٰ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, he signalled to them.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: He wrote to them; that is the «وحي».
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿أَن سَبِّحُواْ بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيّاً﴾.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: Pray. This is well known in the language, and from it prayer is called «سُبْحة».

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يٰيَحْيَىٰ خُذِ ٱلْكِتَابَ بِقُوَّةٍٍ﴾.
There is an ellipsis (ḥadhf) in the speech, because the addressee knows [what is meant].
The meaning is: So We granted him Yaḥyā, and We said: O Yaḥyā, take the Book with strength.
Mujāhid said: That is, with earnestness.
Someone else said: That is, with earnestness and help from Allah.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ ٱلْحُكْمَ صَبِيّاً﴾.
ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Maʿmar informed us; he said: It reached us that the boys said to Yaḥyā when he was a child: "Come, let us play." He said: "We were not created for play." So He, Exalted be His praise, said: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ ٱلْحُكْمَ صَبِيّاً﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the sense of his words.
ʿIkrima said: «الحُكْم» is understanding (sound intellect).
Qatāda said: He was two or three years old.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَحَنَاناً مِّن لَّدُنَّا﴾.
Shuʿba related from Simāk from ʿIkrima, who said: «الحَنان» is mercy.
And so it is according to the lexicographers; its origin is from the yearning (حنين) of the she-camel for her young. Ṭarafa said:
أَبَا مُنْذِرٍ أَفْنَيْتَ فَاسْتَبْقِ بَعْضَنا * حَنَانيْكَ بَعْضُ الشَّرِّ أهَوْنُ مِنْ بَعْضِ
(Abū Mundhir, you have destroyed [us], so spare some of us — mercy upon mercy! Some evil is lighter than other.)
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَزَكَاةً وَكَانَ تَقِيّاً﴾.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: «الزكاة» is the pure, upright intellect.
Qatāda said: «الزكاة» is charity.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَسَلاَمٌ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوْمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَياً﴾.
Qatāda related from al-Ḥasan, who said: When Yaḥyā met Jesus, peace be upon them both, Yaḥyā said to him: "You are better than I." Jesus said: "Rather, you are better than I: Allah greeted you with peace, while I greeted myself with peace."

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱذْكُرْ فِي ٱلْكِتَابِ مَرْيَمَ إِذِ ٱنتَبَذَتْ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا مَكَاناً شَرْقِياً﴾.
That is, she withdrew and went far away.
And «نبَذتُ الشيءَ» means: I threw it away.
It has been said: She made for the place of sunrise, to wash herself after menstruation.
And it has been said: to be alone in worship.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَرْسَلْنَآ إِلَيْهَآ رُوحَنَا﴾.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: Gabriel, Allah bless him and grant him peace.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view, because someone else said: it is Jesus.
What indicates this [i.e. that it is Gabriel] is the saying of the Exalted ﴿فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهَا بَشَراً سَوِيّاً﴾, whereas Jesus is a human being.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَتْ إِنِّيۤ أَعُوذُ بِٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ مِنكَ إِن كُنتَ تَقِيّاً﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: That is, if you are God-fearing, you will take heed of my seeking refuge in Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, from you.
Someone else said: «إن» has the sense of «ما» (negation: "you are not God-fearing"). The first is preferable.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَنَاْ رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِيَهَبَ لَكِ غُلاَماً زَكِيّاً﴾.
It is also read ﴿لأهَبَ لَكِ﴾ ("that I may give you").
The meaning of «لأهَبَ», with the hamza, is construed according to the sense, i.e. He [Allah] said: I sent him so that I may give you.
And «ليهَبَ» without the hamza may have the sense of the hamzated form, the hamza then being lightened.
And it has been said: The meaning is: Allah sent me so that He may give you.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَتْ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِي غُلاَمٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِي بَشَرٌ﴾.
That is, no one has touched me by way of marriage; ﴿وَلَمْ أَكُ بَغِيّاً﴾, i.e. no one has come near me outside the bounds of marriage.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ كَذٰلِكَ قَالَ رَبُّكَ هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ﴾.
That is, the matter is as you have been told.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَحَمَلَتْهُ فَٱنْتَبَذَتْ بِهِ مَكَاناً قَصِيّاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, remote.
Al-Kisāʾī said: One says «قَصَا يقصو», i.e. it became far; «أقصاه اللهُ»; and «أَقْصَى الشَّيءَ»: he put it far away.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَجَآءَهَا ٱلْمَخَاضُ إِلَىٰ جِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid said: That is, the labour pains drove her.
Al-Kisāʾī said: It is from «جاء» (to come): «جئتُ بهِ» (I brought him) and «أَجَأْتُهُ» (I made him come).
This agrees with the view of Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid, because when it drove her to go to the trunk of the palm tree, it brought her to it. Zuhayr said:
وَجَارٍ سَار مُعْتَمِداً إليكُم * أَجَاءَتْهُ المَخَافَةُ والرَّجَاءُ
(And a protégé who journeyed, making straight for you — fear and hope drove him [to you].)
And «المخاض» is pregnancy [labour].
Abū ʿUbayd said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us from Sufyān: Mujāhid said: The fruit of the palm tree was ʿajwa dates.
Someone else said: It was a trunk without a crown, and that was in winter; so Allah made a crown grow for it and created fresh dates on it.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: She conceived and gave birth in a single hour.
Someone else said: She remained [pregnant] eight months, and that was a sign, because no child born at eight months survives.
Abū Isḥāq said: The saying of the Exalted ﴿فَأَجَآءَهَا المَخَاضُ إلى جِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾ indicates a long stay, and Allah knows best.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿قَالَتْ يٰلَيْتَنِي مِتُّ قَبْلَ هَـٰذَا﴾.
That is, had I been given the choice between death and this, I would have chosen death.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَكُنتُ نَسْياً مَّنسِيّاً﴾.
ʿIkrima said: That is, a discarded menstrual rag.
And «النَّسْي» according to the lexicographers is of two kinds:
The first: what has stayed a long time and so been forgotten.
The other: the contemptible thing that is paid no heed.
Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb read: ﴿وكنتُ نِسْئاً﴾,
and Nawf read ﴿وكنْتُ نَسْاً﴾.
This is from «نَسَأ الله في أَجلِهِ», i.e. He postponed [his term].
Ḥammād ibn Salama said: ʿĀṣim said to me: "How do you read «فَأَجَأَهَا»?" I said: "I read it ﴿فأَجَاءَهَا﴾." He said: "It is only «فاجَأ», from «المفاجأة» (taking by surprise)."

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِن تَحْتِهَآ﴾.
Thus it is related of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, that they read ﴿مَنْ﴾ with a fatḥa ("he who was beneath her"), and interpreted it as being Jesus, peace be upon him.
And Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAmr ibn Maymūn and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ ("from beneath her"), and explained it as being Gabriel, Allah bless him and grant him peace.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Gabriel was below her, and he called to her from that place: ﴿أَلاَّ تَحْزَنِي قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيّاً﴾.
Sufyān related from Abū Isḥāq from al-Barāʾ, who said: «السَّرِيّ» is the stream, the small river.
And so it is in the speech of the Arabs; Labīd said:
فَتَوَسَّطَا عُرْضَ السَّرِيِّ وَصَدَّعَا * مَسْجُورَةً مُتَجاوزاً قُلاَّمُهَا
(The two [wild asses] went into the middle of the stream's breadth and split through a brimming pool whose reeds grew thick together.)

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَقُولِيۤ إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ صَوْماً﴾.
Salmān al-Taymī related from Anas, who said: silence.
[Translator's note: the source has «سَلْمان التيمي»; the well-known transmitter from Anas is Sulaymān al-Taymī (سليمان). Translated as written.]
That is well known in the language: anyone who abstains from speech or food is called «صائم», as the poet said:
خَيْلٌ صِيَامٌ وخَيْلٌ غَيْرُ صَائِمَةٍ * تَحْتَ العَجَاجِ وَأُخْرَى تَعْلُكُ اللُّجُمَا
(Horses standing still and horses not still beneath the dust of battle, and others champing at the bits.)
«صيام» [here means] holding back from movement, motionless.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ يٰمَرْيَمُ لَقَدْ جِئْتِ شَيْئاً فَرِيّاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, grave.
Saʿīd ibn Masʿada [al-Akhfash] said: That is, fabricated, invented.
One says «فَرَيتُ» and «أَفْريتُ» with one meaning.
Quṭrub said: Abū Khayra al-ʿAdawī claimed that «الفَرِيّ» is the new among water-skins.
Quṭrub said: So it is as though the meaning of «فَرِيّ» is novel and new, not done before. He said: And it is as though the meaning of «افترى على الله» is: he came with a novel, new thing that had not existed.
Abū ʿUbayda said: «فريّ» is wondrous.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأُخْتَ هَارُونَ مَا كَانَ أَبُوكِ ٱمْرَأَ سَوْءٍ﴾.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: Hārūn was a righteous man among their people, so they said: O you who resemble Hārūn.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is strengthened by the ḥadīth traced back to the Prophet (marfūʿ): "They used to name themselves after their prophets and the righteous among them."
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمَا كَانَتْ أُمُّكِ بَغِيّاً﴾.
That is, a wanton woman; and «البغاء» is fornication.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ﴾.
The meaning is: She pointed to Jesus, [indicating] that they should speak to him. This is indicated by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿قَالُواْ كَيْفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَن كَانَ فِي ٱلْمَهْدِ صَبِيّاً﴾.
It has been said: «كان» here is redundant (zāʾida), because all people have at some time been like this.
And it has been said: «كان» has the sense of "occurred" and "was created".
And it has been said: It carries the sense of a condition, i.e. one who is a child — how can we speak to him?

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ إِنِّي عَبْدُ ٱللَّهِ آتَانِيَ ٱلْكِتَابَ وَجَعَلَنِي نَبِيّاً. وَجَعَلَنِي مُبَارَكاً أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُ﴾.
Sufyān related from Simāk from ʿIkrima concerning the saying of the Exalted ﴿آتَانِي الكِتَابَ﴾ that he said: He has decreed that He will give it to me.
And it has been said that the meaning of ﴿وَأَوْصَانِي بِٱلصَّلاَةِ وَٱلزَّكَاةِ﴾
is: He enjoined upon me prayer and purity.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿ذٰلِكَ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ﴾. [verse 34]
That is, that one who said this is Jesus son of Mary, the servant of Allah.
[Translator's note: the source repeats «الذي الذي» (dittography); rendered once.]
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قَوْلَ ٱلْحَقِّ ٱلَّذِي فِيهِ يَمْتُرُونَ﴾.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us; he said: Salama narrated to us; he said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us; he said: Maʿmar informed us from Qatāda concerning the saying of the Exalted ﴿ذٰلِكَ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ قَوْلَ ٱلْحَقِّ ٱلَّذِي فِيهِ يَمْتُرُونَ﴾ that he said: "The Children of Israel gathered and put forward four men from among them, each people putting forward its scholar, and they disputed about Jesus when he was raised up. One of them said: He is Allah, who came down to earth, gave life to whom He gave life and caused to die whom He caused to die, then ascended to heaven — and these are the Jacobites. He said: The [other] three said: You have lied.
Then two of them said to the third: Speak about him. He said: He is the son of Allah — and these are the Nestorians. He said: The two said: You have lied.
Then the two said to the other: Speak about him! He said: He is the third of three: Allah is a god, he is a god, and his mother is a god — and these are the 'Israelites', the kings of the Christians.
The fourth said: You have lied; rather he is the servant of Allah and His messenger, His spirit and His word — and these are the Muslims. Each man of them had followers in what he said, and they fought, and they prevailed over the Muslims. That is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَقْتُلُونَ الَّذِينَ يَأْمُرُونَ بِالقِسْطِ مِنَ النَّاسِ﴾."
Qatāda said: And they are those about whom Allah said ﴿فاختلف الأحزاب من بينهم﴾: they differed about him and became factions.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَوْيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن مَّشْهَدِ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍٍ﴾.
Mubārak related from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Day of Resurrection.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِرْ يَوْمَ يَأْتُونَنَا﴾.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda, who said: That, by Allah, is the Day of Resurrection: they heard when hearing did not benefit them, and they saw when seeing did not benefit them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning according to the lexicographers is: How well they hear and how well they see on the Day of Resurrection! Because they will have witnessed with their own eyes that which leaves them no need of reflection or deliberation.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَأَنْذِرْهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْحَسْرَةِ إِذْ قُضِيَ ٱلأَمْرُ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ وَهُمْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.
Sufyān related from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: "When the people of Paradise have settled in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire, death will be brought in the form of a black-and-white ram. A call will go out: 'O people of Paradise!' and they will crane their necks to look. Then a call will go out: 'O people of the Fire!' and they will crane their necks to look. It will be said: 'Do you know this?' They will say: 'Yes, this is death' — and there will be none of them but recognises it. Then it will be slaughtered between Paradise and the Fire, and it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, eternity with no death in it; and O people of the Fire, eternity with no death in it.' That is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنْذِرْهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْحَسْرَةِ إِذْ قُضِيَ ٱلأَمْرُ﴾."
Abū Muʿāwiya related from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His saying ﴿وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ وَهُمْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, that he said: in this world.
And Usāma ibn Aḥmad narrated to us; he said: Hārūn ibn Saʿīd al-Aylī narrated to us; he said: Anas ibn ʿIyāḍ narrated to me; he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr informed me, and from Abū Salama, from Abū Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and made to stand on the Bridge (al-Ṣirāṭ). Then it will be said: 'O people of Paradise!' and they will look out, afraid and fearful that they are to be taken out of the place they are in. Then it will be said: 'O people of the Fire!' and they will look out, glad and rejoicing, hoping to be taken out of the place they are in. It will be said: 'Do you know this?' They will say: 'Yes, our Lord, this is death.' Then it will be ordered and slaughtered on the Bridge, and it will be said: 'O people of Paradise, eternity in what you find, with no death in it ever.'"
[Translator's note: «وعن أبي سلمة» ("and from Abū Salama") is as in the source; the usual chain is "Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr, from Abū Salama".]

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱذْكُرْ فِي ٱلْكِتَابِ إِبْرَاهِيمََ﴾.
The meaning is: And mention in the Book that has been sent down to you — which is the Qurʾān — the story of Abraham and his account.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ صِدِّيقاً نَّبِيّاً﴾.
«صِدِّيق» is taken from «الصِّدْق» (truthfulness), and carries the sense of intensiveness and frequency. One who affirms the truth of Allah, His prophets and His obligations, and acts upon them, is called «صِدِّيق»; and from this Abū Bakr was called al-Ṣiddīq.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَبَتِ لاَ تَعْبُدِ ٱلشَّيْطَانََ﴾.
The meaning is: Do not obey him in the unbelief and disobedience he commands you to, for then you would be in the position of one who worships him.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتهِ لأَرْجُمَنَّكَ﴾ — with words.
Abū Jaʿfar said: That is well known in the language; one says «رَجَمَه» and «رَمَاهُ» when one has reviled him; and from this is the saying of the Exalted ﴿والَّذِينَ يَرْمُون المُحْصَنَاتِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَٱهْجُرْنِي مَلِيّاً﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid said: That is, for a while.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, for a long time.
ʿIkrima said: That is, for an age.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, safe, with no harm reaching you from me.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view according to the lexicographers is that it has the sense of a period of time, an age.
Al-Kisāʾī said: One says «هجرتهُ ملِيّاً، ومِلْوَةً، ومُلْوَةً، ومَلاَوَةً، ومُلاَوَةً» (I shunned him for a long while).
Abū Jaʿfar said: From this is «تملَّ حَبِيبَك», i.e. live with him for a long time; and from it «أمليتُ له» (I gave him respite); and from it night and day are called «المَلَوان», as the poet said:
* أمَلَّ عَليْها بالبِلَى المَلَوَانِ *
(Night and day have long worked decay upon it.)

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكَ سَأَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّيۤ إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِي حَفِيّاً﴾.
«الحفيّ» is the kind, gracious one.
One says «حَفِيَ بهِ» and «تحفَّى» when one has treated him kindly.
That is, He used to answer me when I called upon Him.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَوَهَبْنَا لَهْمْ مِّن رَّحْمَتِنَا وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيّاًً﴾.
That is, We preserved for them good praise.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is well known in the language that «اللسان» (the tongue) is put in place of speech, because speech is produced by it, as the poet said:
إِنِّي أَتَانِي لِسَانٌ لاَ أُسَرُّ بِهَا * مِنْ عَلْو لا عَجَبٌ مِنْها وَلاَ سَخَرُ
(A "tongue" [i.e. a report] has come to me in which I take no pleasure, from on high — no wonder at it, nor mockery.)
